title: Align SDK snippets across Python/TS/Go for auth, retries, streaming, and structured output
author: Wei Chen
body: ## Summary This PR aligns canonical Hosted API snippets across Python/TypeScript/Go for the onboarding checklist steps (auth, retries/timeouts, streaming, structured output). The primary goal is to ensure that the snippets: (1) all use the same terminology and environment variable conventions, (2) all demonstrate the same production-safe defaults (timeouts + retries w/ backoff), and (3) all match the feature set we reference from the Console checklist deep links (streaming + structured output). ## Context / Motivation We had drift between language guides that made onboarding inconsistent (e.g., TS showed streaming but no retries, Python showed retries but no timeout, Go used different env vars). This PR is part of ENG-23121 to keep checklist-linked snippets in sync across SDKs. ## What changed (high level) - Standardized auth across docs to `REDWOOD_API_KEY` (and explicitly mention project-scoped keys). - Added consistent retry guidance in all three languages (retry transient errors; respect `Retry-After` for 429; cap total attempts). - Streaming examples updated to use the same event semantics + recommend reconnect behavior. - Structured output examples updated to use the same JSON schema and the same field names in responses across docs. - Reorganized snippets to keep the onboarding path consistent: "First request" -> "Retries/timeouts" -> "Streaming" -> "Structured output". ## Notable snippet updates ### Auth (consistent across all guides) - Docs now show the same setup: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` - Removed references to older `RW_API_KEY` and `REDWOOD_TOKEN` env vars (those still work in some internal tooling, but onboarding docs should be canonical). ### Retries/timeouts (consistent story) - Recommend: timeout on every request; retry only idempotent requests; exponential backoff + jitter; do not retry on 401/403/404. - Clarified 429 guidance: treat as quota/rate limit, read `Retry-After` when present, and surface clear logs. Python (excerpt): ```python import os from redwood import Redwood from redwood.errors import ApiError, RateLimitError, TimeoutError client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"], timeout_s=30, max_retries=4) try: resp = client.chat.completions.create( model="redwood/verified-llama", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}], ) except RateLimitError as e: # respect retry-after; consider queueing/backpressure raise except TimeoutError: raise except ApiError as e: # don't retry 4xx auth/validation; retry transient 5xx handled by SDK defaults raise ``` TypeScript (excerpt): ```ts import { Redwood } from "@redwood-ai/sdk"; const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY!, timeoutMs: 30_000, maxRetries: 4 }); const resp = await client.chat.completions.create({ model: "redwood/verified-llama", messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Say hello" }], }); ``` Go (excerpt): ```go client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"), redwood.WithTimeout(30*time.Second), redwood.WithMaxRetries(4)) ctx := context.Background() resp, err := client.ChatCompletions.Create(ctx, &redwood.ChatCompletionRequest{ Model: "redwood/verified-llama", Messages: []redwood.ChatMessage{{Role: "user", Content: "Say hello"}}, }) ``` ### Streaming - Aligned the docs on the same expected streaming behavior and how to handle disconnects (surface partial output, allow retry with application-level dedupe, and log request IDs). - Clarified that streaming is SSE and can be affected by proxies/timeouts; recommend configuring client and server timeouts. TypeScript streaming (excerpt): ```ts const stream = await client.chat.completions.stream({ model: "redwood/verified-llama", messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Write a haiku about batching" }], }); for await (const event of stream) { if (event.type === "token") process.stdout.write(event.token); if (event.type === "error") throw event.error; } ``` ### Structured output - Replaced ad-hoc examples with a single schema used across all languages and ensured the response parsing blocks are parallel. - Added a note to validate output and to treat schema violations as recoverable (retry w/ a stronger system message) rather than silently accepting malformed JSON. Example schema (used in all three pages): ```json { "type": "object", "properties": { "title": {"type": "string"}, "summary": {"type": "string"}, "severity": {"type": "string", "enum": ["low", "medium", "high"]} }, "required": ["title", "summary", "severity"], "additionalProperties": false } ``` ## Changed areas/files (representative) - `docs/api/quickstart/first-request.mdx` - `docs/api/guides/retries-and-timeouts.mdx` - `docs/api/guides/streaming.mdx` - `docs/api/guides/structured-output.mdx` - `docs/_snippets/python/*.mdx` - `docs/_snippets/typescript/*.mdx` - `docs/_snippets/go/*.mdx` - `tools/snippet-verify/*` (minor updates to keep verification deterministic) ## Testing - `pnpm test` (docs unit tests) - `pnpm build` (site build) - `pnpm snippets:verify` (compiles/runs snippet harness for python/ts/go) ## Rollout / Notes - No product behavior changes; documentation-only. - This PR is intentionally strict about env var naming and option defaults to match the upcoming Console checklist deep links. ## Follow-ups - Add a small "Request IDs" section to each language guide once SDKs expose a consistent accessor (tracked in SDK repos; not part of this docs PR).
conversation: Monica Patel (review): The direction looks good. Two asks: (1) can we keep `timeout_s` / `timeoutMs` / `WithTimeout` called out explicitly in each snippet (right now Python has it but TS/Go examples in retries section are a bit terse), and (2) make sure we’re not implying we retry non-idempotent operations by default. Also: please align the model string with what Hosted API onboarding uses elsewhere (either `redwood/verified-llama` or the specific catalog entry).

Wei Chen (author): Ack. I’ll expand TS/Go retries section to show timeout + maxRetries in the constructor/options, and I’ll add a short note that our examples assume idempotent chat completion requests and that callers should be careful with side-effecting tool calls. I’ll keep the model string consistent with the onboarding path (`redwood/verified-llama`).

Dana Lo (review): Streaming example: can we avoid the old `on('data')` style? Using `for await` matches the SDK and reads cleaner. Also, the structured output page currently shows `response.output_text` in one place and `response.outputText` in another — can you make sure each language uses the right accessor and we don’t accidentally copy TS casing into Python docs?

Wei Chen (author): Updated TS streaming to `for await` and fixed the casing/accessors across the structured output page. I also ran `snippets:verify` locally to make sure the updated snippets compile.

Ibrahim Khan (review): +1 overall. One more nit: the retry section says "retry transient errors" but doesn’t define them. Can we include a small bullet list (429/408/5xx/network timeouts) and explicitly say "do not retry 401" (this keeps Support happy; see SUP-9244 pattern)?
Wei Chen (author): Added the bullet list and explicit "don’t retry 401/403". Also added a short sentence about 429 meaning rate limit/quota and respecting `Retry-After`.

Elliot Price (review): Please ensure the docs pages link targets and headings remain stable (Console deep links will use these anchors). Specifically, don’t rename the H2s without adding explicit `id=` attributes. Also, can you add a sentence that prompts are not collected in onboarding telemetry (folks conflate docs with product analytics)?

Wei Chen (author): Added explicit heading IDs on the modified H2s and avoided renaming existing anchors. Added a privacy note in the onboarding context callout: "Redwood onboarding telemetry does not collect prompt or completion content."
Wei Chen (author): Fixed missing import and re-ran snippet verification. Pushed follow-up commit.
Monica Patel (review): Approved. Thanks for making the retries section consistent across all languages.
Elliot Price (review): Approved. Heading IDs + stability callouts look good.
